2. The brief case of the prosecution is that:
On 03082021 at about 5.15 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Creta Car bearing registration No.KA Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
1 05NA1810 drove the same on Mahalakshmi Layout, 12th cross, from Panchamukhi temple towards Mahalakshmi Entrance gate in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to Honda Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA 41/EC 9457 which was coming in the opposite direction. Due to the impact the rider and pillion rider fell down along with vehicle. The rider Kum. Neha sustained simple injuries and the pillion rider Kum. Deepa Shree sustained grievous head injuries and later she succumbed to death. Thereby the accused is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
3. Upon taking cognizance, case came to be registered against accused for the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC. The accused appeared before the court through his counsel & got enlarged on bail. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 Charge sheet copies furnished to the accused and thereby provision U/s.207 of Cr.P.C. duly complied with. 
4. Plea came to be framed for the offences U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC. for which accused pleaded not guilty claimed to be tried. 
5. During the course of trial, the prosecution has examined P.W.1 to 8 and got exhibited documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11. On completion of prosecution side evidence, the statement of accused U/s.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded and the accused denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against him and did not choose to lead any defence evidence. 
6. Heard arguments on both sides. The learned APP contended that in the instant case the complainant being a hearsay witness has deposed about the accident, the version of the complaint was supported by eye witness i.e., P.W.2 and his evidence was not shaken in cross examination.
The either witness P.W.3 also supported the accident and vehicles involved in the accident, both P.W.2 and 3 identified the accused, the P.W.4 being the rider of the two wheeler also supports the case of the prosecution and their evidence was corroborated by investigating officer and mahazar witness. The prosecution has C.C.No.4111/2021 established the fact of accident and negligence on the part of the accused driver and hence pray for conviction. To counter the same the learned counsel for the accused contended that the P.W.1 is a hearsay witness and he is of no importance to the case of the prosecution. P.W.2 is examined as eye witness and he has deposed contrary to the version of the investigating officer with regard to width of the road and accident spot. The said witness speaks about the presence of auto and damage caused to auto. The said auto driver or auto is not mentioned in charge sheet, why the said person was left out, this raises question mark about the genuineness of the case of the prosecution. The other eye witness clearly amdits that he has not seen the accident live and accident has taken place before he come out of hte shop, which means he cannot say about accident. The P.W.4 being the rider of the motor cycle deposed that she was proceeding in extreme left, but the version of the investigating officer is different from P.W.4. 
Moreover she is the friend of the deceased and she comes in the category of interested witness. The other witnesses examined are police officers who deposed about their duty. There are certain material contradictions in the case of the prosecution and that raises doubt about the case of the Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
2 prosecution itself. The C.C.No.4111/2021 prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and hence pray for acquittal. 
7. In view of the rival submissions and depositions the following points arise for my consideration in the instant case:
1.Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 03082021 at about 5.15 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Creta Car bearing registration No.KA05NA1810 drove the same on Mahalakshmi Layout, 12 th cross, from Panchamukhi temple towards Mahalakshmi Entrance in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life,
thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.279 of IPC? 
2.Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place the accused being the driver of the said vehicle, drove his vehicle in the above said manner. While so driving his vehicle dashed to Honda Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA41/EC9457 which was coming in the opposite direction. Due to the impact the rider and pillion rider fell down along with vehicle. The rider Kum. Neha sustained simple injuries and the pillion rider Kum. 
Deepa shree sustained grievous head injuries and later she succumbed to death,
thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.304(A) of IPC?
4. What order? 
C.C.No.4111/2021 8. My answer to the above points are as under:
POINT No.1: IN THE NEGATIVE POINT No.2: IN THE NEGATIVE POINT No.3: AS PER THE FINAL ORDER For the following REASONS 9. POINT No.1 and 2: For the sake of convenience and to avoid repetition of facts, these points are taken up for common discussion to have brevity.
10. It is the case of the prosecution that on 03082021 at about 5.15 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Creta Car bearing registration No.KA05NA 1810 drove the same on Mahalakshmi Layout, 12 th cross, from Panchamukhi temple towards Mahalakshmi Entrance in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to Honda Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA41/EC9457 which was coming in the opposite direction. Due to the impact the rider and pillion rider fell down along with vehicle. The rider Kum. Neha sustained simple injuries and the pillion rider Kum. Deepa shree sustained grievous head injuries and later she succumbed to death. Thereby the accused C.C.No.4111/2021 is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC.

3 11. In order to prove its case the prosecution examined 8 witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.8 and marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
12. C.W.1/ Yoganand is examined as P.W.1 who is the complainant of this case. He deposed that on 03082021 his daughter left home at 11.00 a.m. in his Scooter bearing registration No.KA41 EH1278 and went to her friend's house at Laggere and from there they went for shopping and at around 5.15 p.m. when they were coming near Srinviasa temple road, one car bearing registration No.KA05/NA1810 came in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to her daughter's vehicle. The sound of the accident was heard till one kilometer. He further deposed that his daughter was a pillion rider at the time of accident. Due to accident her friend Sneha was riding the scooter also sustained injuries. Later his daughter was shifted to Sanjivini hospital and he received information their he went and later shifted her to Sparsh hospital. But his daughter succumbed to death. In that regard he has lodged complaint before Rajajinagar police station against car driver. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 During his crossexamination by accused counsel he deposed that he received information from Rajajinagar police station at around 6.00 p.m. when he visited hospital his daughter was not in a position to talk. He admits the accident spot is a two way road without divider. 
He also admits about the density of traffic in the said road. he denied the suggestions with regard to collusion with auto. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
13. C.W.2 / Anand is examined as P.W.2 who is the eye witness of this case. He deposed that on 03 082021 at about 5.15 p.m. while he was standing in front of his shop two persons were riding in their two wheeler from Mahalakshmi entrance towards panchamukhi temple, at taht time one Creta car was coming from opposite direction, it came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to two wheeler, due to the impact the pillion rider sustained grievous injuries, the car dashed to front portion of the two wheeler. He deposed the registration numbers of the vehicles and identified the accused before the court. He further deposed that police conducted mahazar in his presence. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 During his crossexamination he deposed that the said road is having a width of 30ft and it is a two way road. He admits about existence of footpath on both sides and also admits about high density of traffic in the said road. He deposed that his shop is situated at a distance of 20ft from accident spot. When he was questioned about rough sketch map he deposed that when he is seen the incident the scooter was going in the left side of the road and not in the middle of the road. He deposed that accident has taken place at a distance of 5ftt from the edge of the road and deposed that in the sketch police mentioned wrong information. He denied the suggestions with regard to negligence on the part of the two wheeler. 
He further deposed that a auto was proceeding in front of the car and the said auto was also damaged in the accident. He further deposed that auto was behind the two wheeler. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel and also deposed that at the time of accident it was raining. 
14. C.W.3/ Kishore Kumar is examined as P.W.3 who is the eye witness of this case. He deposed that on 03082021 at about 5.00 p.m. while he was inside the shop accident has taken place, in front of Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
4 his shop. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 Honda Dio scooter was proceeding towards panchamukhi temple, creta car come from opposite direction and dashed to two wheeler and due to impact the pillion rider of the two wheeler sustained head injuries. He send them to Sanjivini hospital. Later police told him about the death of the pillion rider. He identified the accused before the court. 
During his crossexamination by accused counsel he deposed that the said road is a two way road and after 5.00 p.m. normally the traffic is heavy on the said road. He admits that due to high density of vehicles riding vehicle in high speed was not possible. He admits that he came to know about the accident after hearing the sound. He admits he has not seen the accident live. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
15. C.W.4/ Kum. Neha is examined as P.W.4 who is the eye witness of this case. She deposed that the deceased is her friend. On 03082021 at about 5.15 p.m. she and her friend was proceeding towards panchamukhi temple in their scooter and when she came near Lakshmi battery shop the creta car which was coming from opposite direction and dashed to the right side. Due to the impact they fell down and her friend sustained head C.C.No.4111/2021 injury. Later they were sent to Sanjivini hospital and identified the accused before the court. 
During her crossexamination by accused counsel she deposed that on the said day they went to KFC to have food and when they were proceeding towards their houe accident ahs taken place. She admits it is a two way traffic road and normally heavy traffic is found on the said road. She admits driving vehicle in high speed is not possible in the said road. She deposed that she was proceeding in the left side of the road. She further admits the car was coming in the left side of their lane. She denied the suggestions with regard to dashing her scooter to car. She denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
16. C.W.5/ Vinay is examined as P.W.5 who is the mahazar witness of this case. He deposed that on 04 082021 police asked him to become a witness for mahazar when he agreed he was taken near Exide battery shop at Mahalakshmi layout and they told him that yesterday an accident has taken place between scooter and creta car and in that regard they conducted mahazar between 1.00 p.m.
to 2.00 p.m. and obtained his signature on mahazar and rough sketch map. The said witness was not crossexamined by the accused counsel. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 17. C.W.17/ Srinivasa Gowda is examined as P.W.6 who is the 1st Investigating Officer of this case. 
He deposed that on 04082021 on the basis of information given by C.W.1 he received the written complaint and registered the case in Crime No.55/21 against the accused. On the same day he visited the accident spot and conducted spot mahazar and prepared one rough sketch and recorded the statement of C.W.1. At this stage he received the information that the injured was succumbed to death. As this case is a serious case, he handed over the case file to C.W.18 for further investigation.

5 During his crossexamination by the accused counsel he admits that it is a two way road and generally has heavy traffic. He admits that it is not possible to drive the vehicle in high speed at evening hours. He admits that he has not obtained the statements of the shop owners near the accident spot. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
18. C.W.19/ Sridhar is examined as P.W.7 who is the 3rd Investigating Officer of this case. He deposed that he received the case file from C.W.18 and conducted further investigation. He has given request letter to the concerned vehicle inspector and the concerned inspector C.C.No.4111/2021 conducted the vehicle inspection. He issued Sec.133 notice to the owner and received reply to the said notice. He has arrested the accused and released him on bail. He has recorded the statement of eye witnesses C.W.1 to 4. He released the vehicle after obtaining indemnity bond. He received the postmortem report and received the motor vehicle inspection report. After completion of investigation he has filed the charge sheet against the accused. 
During his crossexamination he deposed that he has enquired the local shop owners, but he has not taken their statements. He admits it is a two way road, but denies the suggestions that there is a high density of traffic. He admits BMTC buses also ply in the said road. He admits the footpath is situated at a distance of 15ft from the center of the road. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
19. C.W.18/ Smt. Nagarathnamma is examined as P.W.8 who is the 2nd Investigating Officer of this case. She deposed that on 13082021 she received information from hospital about the death of the injured. Immediately she sent requisition to court to adopt Sec.304(A) and later he visited the hospital, the family members opted for organ donation. He permitted the C.C.No.4111/2021 same and later conducted inquest mahazar on the same day she obtained further statement of witnesses and later handed over the case file to C.W.19 for further investigation. During her cross examination by the accused counsel she denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
20. Out of the documents marked for prosecution Ex.P.1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar vehicle photo, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar. Ex.P.4 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.5 is the FIR,
Ex.P.6 is the 133 notice, Ex.P.7 is the reply, Ex.P.8 is the Postmortem Report, Ex.P.9 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.10 is the Indemnity bond and Ex.P.11 is the inquest mahazar. 
21. In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of the Car drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident due to which the victim succumbed to death and prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 &
304(A) of IPC. Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused C.C.No.4111/2021 was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person. For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence. It must be more than mere carelessness or error of judgment. The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
6 human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. 
22. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide. 
23. In the instant case the prosecution has examined 8 witnesses to prove their case. Among them P.W.1 is the complainant who is an hearsay witness, P.W.2 to 4 are the eye witnesses, P.W.5 is the mahazar witness, and P.W.6 to 8 are the investigating officers. In the instant case the prosecution is relying on P.W.2 to 4 i.e., eye witnesses and investigating officer. The learned C.C.No.4111/2021 APP contended that all the eye witnesses supported their case and their evidence is corroborated with the evidence of investigating officer and they have proved their case as per their version. 
24. In the instant case the accused is the driver of the alleged vehicle the said fact is not disputed by the defence. The defence also did not dispute the alleged accident between the Dio scooter and creta car. The defence is not disputing the death of the deceased Deepa shree. The defence is disputing the allegation of rash and negligent driving on the part of the accused. 
25. To prove the rash and negligent act of the accused the prosecution has relied its case on P.W.2 to 4. P.W.2 in his chief examination deposed that the accused driver drove his car in a rash and negligent manner. He did not explain in what manner the car was driven and what is the negligence which he has noticed. The other eye witness deposed that the accused drove his car in high speed and dashed to two wheeler. The P.W.4 did not depose anything about either high speed or negligence she simply deposed that the accused came in opposite direction and dashed to their scooter. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 26. To bring home the culpability of accused under section 279 and 304(A) IPC, it is necessary to know the relevant provisions of law which reads as follows:
Section 279. Rash driving or riding on a public way:
Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. 
27. Upon bare perusal of the above provision in order to come to conclusion that accused has committed the offence punishable under above section, the prosecution must establish the following:
Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
7 1. Person must be driving or riding vehicle in a public way. 
2. He must be driving in a rash and negligent manner. 
3. He must be driving in a manner likely to endanger human life or personal safety of any person. 
28. Upon plain reading of the provision of law i.e., Sec.279 and 304 (A) of IPC , the prosecution has to make out that death is a direct consequence of a rash or C.C.No.4111/2021 negligent act. As per dictionary meaning Rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or doing an act without due consideration whereas negligence connotes want of proper care. A rash act implies an act done by a person with recklessness or with indifference to its consequences, the prosecution must establish that the alleged accused must be conscious of his act and must be aware of the consequences which will take place due to his act and it is not intention one. A negligent act, refers to an act done by a person without taking sufficient precautions or reasonable precautions to avoid its probable mischievous or illegal consequences. The prosecution has contended that accused has committed negligent act due to which the rider of the motor cycle was succumbed to death. 
29. With regard to negligent act the Hon'ble Apex court in "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs State of Andhra Pradesh (decided on 28.07.2000)" , wherein the Court discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:
"A rash act is primarily an over hasty act. It is opposed to a deliberate act. Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution. 
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences. Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and C.C.No.4111/2021 precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular. It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution." 
30. Further, in the case of "Braham Dass Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh (2009) 3 SCC (Cri) 406",
while discussing the legal position with respect to an offence u/s 279/304A, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, interalia observed the following:
"Obviously the foundation in accusations under Section 279 IPC is not negligence. 
Similarly, in Section 304A the stress is on causing death by negligence or rashness. 
Therefore, for bringing in application of either Section 279 or 304A it must be established that there was an element of rashness or negligence. Even if the prosecution version is accepted in toto, there was no evidence led to show that any negligence was involved." 
31. In the instant case, the fact that the accused was driving the vehicle has not been disputed by him and he has not deposed anything in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. Thus, it is Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
8 not in dispute that accused Shreyas was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident. 
Now the prosecution has the burden to prove the rashness and negligence on the part of the accused. To prove the same they have examined P.W.2 to 4 and relied on them. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 32. PW.2 is the eye witness who deposed that he was standing in front of his shop at the time fo accident and he has seen the accident from a distance of 20ft. He contended accused drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner. He contended that the accident has taken place at a distance of 5ft from the left side edge of the road. He disputed the rough sketch map which was prepared by the investigating officer and deposed in clarity that the accident spot is shown in wrong place. 
Unfortunately he is a witness to the spot mahazar and rough sketch as well. According to him accident has taken place at a distance of 15ft from the edge of the road which means exactly in the center of the road. The said witness in his crossexamination also deposed about damage caused to the auto. He deposed about presence of auto at accident spot and involvement of auto in the accident spot. If auto is damaged why it has been not shown in the charge sheet. What constrained the investigating officer from examining the driver of the said auto. He is a material witness to the case of the prosecution. The said witness is not listed in the prosecution witness list. Which raises doubt about the investigation of the case. The same witness in his cross examination clearly admits it is a two way road and normally the road is busy and it has high density of C.C.No.4111/2021 traffic. If that is the scenario what is the negligence on the part of the accused, nothing is deposed by the said witness. When he himself admits the accident has taken place in the center of the road, if the same is considered in feets it is exactly the center lane and not a inch excess to their lane. The prosecution failed to establish the negligence on the part of the accused driver from this witness. 
Moreover a doubt is created with the inclusion of auto into the scene. 
33. P.W.3 the other eye witness deposed that the accused drove his vehicle in high speed and dashed to two wheeler which was coming from opposite direction. Apart from high speed he did not mention anything about negligence. Whether high speed alone constitutes negligence Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled "State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)" 
wherein the Apex Court observed:
"merely because the truck was being driven at a high speed does not bespeak of either "negligence or rashness" by itself. None of the witness examined by the prosecution could give any indication, even approximately, as to what they meant by "high speed". 
High speed is a relative term. It was for the prosecution to bring on record material to establish as to what it meant by high speed in the facts and circumstances of the case. In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of C.C.No.4111/2021 the accused until the contrary is proved. Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions. There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case. 
Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
9 In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur". 
34. In the above said judgment the court has clearly held that mere driving the vehicle in high speed will not amounts to negligence and it is for the prosecution to prove how high speed amounts to negligence. In the case on hand the same witness who deposed about high speed also deposed that the said road where accident has taken place is having a width of 30ft and the said road is a busy road and normally has heavy traffic. When there is a heavy traffic the question of driving the vehicle in high speed is not possible. moreover it is not the case of the prosecution that the accused was so negligent that he drove his vehicle in high speed in a busy road and caused damages to several vehicles in one act, if that is the scenario the version of the prosecution appears to be believable one. 
Unfortunately nothing of such kind is placed before the court and the prosecution did not include the auto which was damaged in the alleged accident. The other eye witness P.W.4 did not depose anything about the negligence on the part of the accused driver. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 35 . Further the prosecution has to prove that the alleged negligent act of the accused is the direct cause of death. The investigating officer did not depose anything about the possession of driving license by the deceased at the time of the accident. There is no mention whether the rider or the pillion rider was wearing a head gear at the time of accident. According to postmortem report the death is a result of head injury sustained. If the said person wear a helmet then there is a chance of avoiding head injury, the prosecution did not place any materials about wearing the head gear. 
36. Further aspect is the victim fell on the footpath after the collusion. As per prosecution sketch map i.e., Ex.P.4 the footpath is at distance of 7ft from the accident spot. Upon perusal of photographs there is a grill over the footpath, whether the victim fly in the air and landed on the footpath and sustained heady injury, none of the witness spoken about the same. Everybody speaks about colluding with the footpath stone, how she landed on footpath, whether the grills came in between the deceased and footpath there is no clarity. These factors raises doubt about the version of the prosecution itself. 
C.C.No.4111/2021 37. The other aspect with regard to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased. Admittedly the deceased is a girl and rider is also a girl, there is a doubt whether they possess valid driving license and she is riding a high speed vehicle. The counsel further contended the deceased was riding a unfit vehicle and due to his negligence the untoward incident has taken place. 
38. Whether the prosecution has established rash and negligent act on the part of the accused. In that regard the Hon'ble Apex court in S. Khader v. N. Gama, has held that the the important criteria for deciding as to whether the driver who caused the accident was rash or negligent would depend upon some of the following factors : They are Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
10 1. Speed of the vehicle (It is only one of the several factors in determining rashness or negligence);
2 . Width of the road;
3. Density of the traffic; and 4. Attempt, if any to overtake the vehicles. 
39. Upon perusal of the records of the instant case though the witness speak about high speed of the vehicle they did not speak about any attempt to over take C.C.No.4111/2021 the other vehicle by accused person. Further all most all witnesses admit about high density of traffic on the said road. 
Which generally raises a presumption that high speed is not possible particularly with regard to four wheeler. Since it consumes more space for passing and violation of the same gathers attention of the general public. Admittedly the said road is quite wider enough for movement of large vehicles, it has a width of 30ft and it is a two way road without any divider. As per the admissions there is a commercial establishment on both sides and there is a provision for parking of vehicles as well, if that aspect is taken into consideration the width of the road is reduced from both sides and it congest the vehicular movement. According to witness the accident has taken place in the middle of the road and according to prosecution it is a head to head collusion. On perusal of the sketch map as per Ex.P.4 the victim has not crossed the center line and it is the accused crossed the center line. As discussed earlier their is a contradiction on this aspect. Negligence is the absence of care and caution whereas culpable rashness results from lack of circumspection. Merely because the car is being driven at a high speed it would be speak of either negligence or rashness. High speed is a relative term and that has to be examined in the light of the facts & circumstances of the C.C.No.4111/2021 case. In the instant case though they speak about speed of the accused none of them speak about the speed of the victim. With the available materials the court cannot come to the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the speed of the accused alone. 
40. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.
